title: Workflows and agents: who owns the control flow

items.stem: Which statement correctly tells an agent apart from a workflow?

options.text: An agent runs on a larger, more capable model, while a workflow runs on a smaller one
In an agent the model decides the steps and when to stop; in a workflow, code written in advance sets the steps
A workflow never calls a language model, while an agent calls one at every step
An agent is allowed to call tools such as a calendar lookup, while a workflow is not allowed to

items.stem: Which of these makerspace features is a workflow rather than an agent?

options.text: The model gets a booking goal plus the tools check_calendar and book_machine, and chooses its own calls until it decides it is done
The model answers a question by choosing between search_manuals and check_calendar, and searches again if the first result is thin
Code looks up the booking, makes one model call to write the confirmation text, then sends it, in that order for every request
The model reads the student's message and decides which tools to use, in what order, and how many times to use them

items.stem: The assistant handles 40 booking confirmations a day. As a fixed workflow, every confirmation takes exactly 2 model calls. As an agent, each confirmation averages 5 model calls, because the model decides each step. How many more model calls per day does the agent version make than the workflow version?
Every booking must go through the same steps in the same order: check the student's training record, check the calendar, then write the booking. Which choice fits best, and why?

options.text: A fixed workflow, because the steps are known in advance and identical each time, so cost is predictable and testing is simple
An agent, because a more flexible system is always the better design, even for a task that never changes
An agent, because letting the model pick the order of steps uses fewer model calls than fixing the order
A fixed workflow, because a workflow can adapt on its own when a student asks something nobody planned for

items.stem: A fixed workflow has three steps: (1) a model call pulls the machine and date out of the student's message, (2) code calls check_calendar with them, (3) a model call writes the reply. Who decided that check_calendar runs right after step 1?

options.text: The model, which chose the tool at the end of step 1 because it judged the calendar was needed next
The team that wrote the code, who fixed the order in advance, so it happens whatever the model outputs
The calendar tool, which signals the program that it is ready to be called
The student, whose message determines the order of steps in each request

items.stem: In a proposed design, one model call reads each student message and outputs a single label, "manual_question" or "booking". Code then runs the fixed pipeline the team built for that label, with the same steps every time. Which description is best?

options.text: An agent, because a language model reads the request and is involved in the process
An agent, because the model's label decides which steps happen next
Neither; a single model call is too small to count as either design
A workflow, because the code owns the sequence and the model only picks among paths built in advance
